cover.deck: I make short, tense games, and tools when the games need them.
cover.bio: Unity developer, C#. My games are built around one strong mechanic: an echo replaying your moves eight seconds later, a wolf that learns from your traps, a world that only exists one colour at a time. Five of them play right here in this page. On the side, six editor tools published on the Asset Store, downloaded more than thirteen thousand times.
cover.note: Games marked “playable here” run inside the page, nothing to install. Keyboard recommended.

eco.hook: Your past catches up with you, eight seconds late.
eco.body: ECO is a puzzle-platformer where every move is recorded and replayed by an echo eight seconds later. A button to hold, a door that needs two: your self from eight seconds ago does the job while you move on. My longest project, playable solo or in co-op, with a level editor whose creations are shared online from inside the game.
eco.long:
ECO is a puzzle-platformer built on a single rule: everything you do is replayed by an echo eight seconds later. A button that must stay pressed, a platform to hold up, a passage that only opens for two: your double from eight seconds ago does the work while you move ahead.

It plays solo or in co-op, and ships with a level editor: levels you build go online from inside the game, and everyone else's show up in the Community menu. Nothing to zip, no folder to find.

It is my longest project. It runs in the browser and on Windows, macOS and Linux.

Session 3 — the echo holds the button while you pass: the line shows what it triggers.
Session 7 — each session changes palette and rule; here, a pillar to hold up.
Session 6 — two characters, two timelines, one clock.
The echo chain: a level is solved by orchestrating several versions of yourself.
inGame: Echo: your inputs are recorded and replayed by a double, eight seconds later.
Local or online co-op: two players, four timelines.
Built-in level editor, online sharing from the game and a Community menu.
Browser, Windows, macOS and Linux builds.

dig-or-die.hook: The wolf learns. The shepherd traps.
dig-or-die.body: An eleven-level puzzle where you place traps before the wolf arrives. It dies, it learns, it comes back avoiding what it saw. Kill it when it thinks it knows everything. Short, tense, pixel art, and playable in the page.
dig-or-die.long:
DIG or DIE is a trap game in eleven levels. You are the shepherd: before each wave you lay spikes, blocks, arrows and traps on the terrain. Then the wolf comes.

The rule that makes the game: the wolf remembers. When it dies on a trap, it returns avoiding it. Traps that worked become decoys, and the solution is never last turn's. Kill it when it thinks it knows everything.

Short, tense, pixel art, with a CRT screen. Keyboard only, straight in the page.
captions: Level 6 — lay your traps on the blocks before the wolf arrives; the inventory below counts what is left.
Level complete — the wolf has learned; next turn it will walk around what killed it.
The bare terrain: each level is a small placement puzzle.
Available traps change from one level to the next.
Eleven levels, one night, an ever smarter wolf.
inGame: Eleven trap-placement levels, a few minutes each.
A wolf that memorises the traps it met and adapts its path.
Pixel art and CRT rendering, keyboard only.

color-gap.hook: A world that only exists one colour at a time.
color-gap.body: A minimalist platformer driven by colour, rhythm and perception. A pristine world fractures into three primary colours; every jump cycles the visible one, and the other two's platforms vanish. Jumping means choosing what exists when you land. Jury's Favorite at the Global Game Jam 2026.
color-gap.long:
Color GAP is a minimalist platformer driven by colour, rhythm and perception. You explore a pristine world built around precise platforming and environmental puzzles. Early on, an event fractures that space and splits reality into three primary colours: yellow, red, blue.

From then on the world exists as overlapping fragments. Every jump shifts your perception and cycles colour masks that only reveal the elements matching the active colour. The platforms are always there, but only one colour is visible at a time. A badly timed jump does not only change your trajectory: it changes what exists when you land.

The music evolves with your actions. Mastering the game means learning when to jump, not only how. Made in 48 hours for the Global Game Jam 2026, where it received the Jury's Favorite award.
captions: The world before the fracture: white, low-poly, silent.
The first colour. The yellow tree only exists while yellow is active.
Every jump cycles the mask: anything not in the active colour disappears.
inGame: Colour cycle triggered on every jump: one colour of platforms visible at a time.
Made in 48 h for the Global Game Jam 2026 — Jury's Favorite.

mirapyde.hook: Freeze time. Your clone replays your moves in reverse.
mirapyde.body: A 2D parkour platformer inside a pyramid. Each room is a closed puzzle: freeze time to create a clone that replays your moves in reverse, and orchestrate two timelines to open the way.
mirapyde.long:
Mirapyde is a 2D platformer built on parkour and time manipulation. Each room is a closed puzzle: one door, one goal, no filler.

The principle: freeze time to create a clone that replays your moves in reverse. That double can press a button while you climb elsewhere, hold a pressure plate, or sync an action you could never do alone. If you fail, you restart instantly.

Clean movement, strict timing, planning: climb the pyramid floor after floor.
captions: One room, one door, one goal.

Traps are unforgiving: you restart immediately.
